name: sebsjames/maths
listed_description: A templated C++20 math library which emphasizes convenience and pleasure for the client programmer (used in mathplot).
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline. README and docs/index.md only say it can replace GLM (templated precision) and covers part of Armadillo and Eigen; no timing, no benchmark directory, no tests with benchmark or perf names. The one Eigen test (tests/mat_4x4_vseigen.cpp) checks that rotate/translate results equal Eigen's and contains no timing code. Directional description only, and the claim words list is empty.

name: sfl library
listed_description: A header-only C++11 library that provides several new or lesser-known containers, some of which can be used in C++20 constant expressions.
reason: Benchmark code exists (benchmark/src/segmented_devector.cpp, unordered_map.cpp, small_unordered_map.cpp; benchmark/makefile uses g++ -std=c++20 -O3 -DNDEBUG; compares sfl::segmented_devector with std::deque and boost::container::deque, 10,000,000 ints, median of 20 runs) but no results are committed or published: README, CHANGELOG and the 56 doc/*.md pages contain only directional wording (devector 'faster insertion and deletion at the front compared to vector', segmented_devector 'a superior alternative to std::deque', CHANGELOG 'Significantly improved performances' for segmented_vector) with no numbers. No open issues; a boostorg/container issue (#324) found by search does not mention sfl. lists.boost.org threads are blocked. Directional claim only, so no record; a verifier with a build environment could run the existing harness (would be new first-party evidence).

name: Snippets
listed_description: Useful code snippets and header-only libraries. Public domain.
reason: No numeric comparison. README only says DG_strlen() and DG_strnlen() 'might be faster than default'. Source comments in DG_misc.h say DG_strnlen is faster than libc strnlen on Windows and FreeBSD, that DG_strlcat/DG_strlcpy are faster than the BSD versions 'in most cases', and that glibc strlen is 'fucking fast', all without numbers, compiler, CPU or harness. No benchmark files in the repo. Directional claims only.

name: sod
listed_description: An Embedded Computer Vision & Machine Learning Library.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. github.com/symisc/sod README says only 'real-time' and 'CPU optimized' and gives no Darknet or OpenCV numbers; a search snippet repeats the site's '5 ~ 15 ms on HD video stream' for the RealNets face detector but that is an absolute figure with no baseline. sod.pixlab.io and blog.pixlab.io are blocked (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so the site docs and blog posts could not be opened. Three searches for SOD versus OpenCV Haar or Darknet found no published comparison. Directional claim only.

name: sphlib
listed_description: Set of implementations of various hash functions, including (listing text truncated at that point).
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline in reachable sources. README (github.com/pornin/sphlib, copy of sphlib 3.0 from 2011; saphir2.com is blocked) only says architecture-specific code 'can reach +30% on the fastest functions' (a self-comparison against its own portable path) and ships a sphspeed tool with no committed results. Search snippets say SUPERCOP (bench.cr.yp.to) benchmarks sphlib implementations and, on aarch64 pi3bplus and pi3aplus, shows OpenSSL faster than sphlib for SHA-256 and SHA-512 (snippet level, opened pages are blocked: bench.cr.yp.to and the viacache.net mirror both EGRESS_BLOCKED), so any SUPERCOP evidence would be against sphlib. A verifier with SUPERCOP data access could look at crypto_hash/shavite3 and groestl rows, where sphlib is an implementation entry.

name: stduuid
listed_description: A C++17 cross-platform implementation for UUIDs.
reason: No numeric comparison. README (single-header implementation of proposal P0959: random, name-based SHA1, system and experimental time-based generators) has no performance section; the repo has no benchmark directory (catch/, cmake/, gsl/, include/, test/); two searches for stduuid versus boost::uuids or libuuid timings found nothing. Not a speed project.
